properties.description: Primary identifier for the codelist. May be a string URI or a structured PropertyValue.
ISO 8601 date when the codelist was last modified.
Web location of a page describing the codelist.
License for the codelist.
Text statement of access conditions for the codelist.

Preferred lexical label for the concept scheme. Required. A single
string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged
values.

**Uniqueness rule.** Each language should appear at most once in the
set of prefLabel values. Two prefLabel values with duplicate `@language`
tags are non-conformant. Consumers may reject or arbitrarily pick one.

**Multilinguality.** For codelists intended for multilingual use,
supply an array of language-tagged values — one per supported locale.
When a bare string is supplied (no `@language` tag), consumers treat
it as untagged and MAY infer the language from the enclosing document's
`@context` or from `schema:inLanguage` on the codelist itself.

**Relationship to skos:altLabel.** Alternate labels (acronyms,
spelling variants, obsolete names) go on `skos:altLabel`, NOT on
`prefLabel`. A concept scheme has exactly one preferred label per
language.
Formal explanation of the meaning or purpose of this concept scheme.
General note about the concept scheme.
Top-level concepts that have no skos:broader in this scheme. Required for hierarchical codelists.
The concept scheme this concept belongs to. Required for CDIF codelist concepts.

Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string,
a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values.
Each language should appear at most once.

**Uniqueness rule.** Each language should appear at most once in the
set of prefLabel values. Two prefLabel values with duplicate `@language`
tags are non-conformant. Consumers may reject or arbitrarily pick one.

**Relationship to skos:altLabel.** Alternate labels (acronyms,
spelling variants, obsolete names) go on `skos:altLabel`, NOT on
`prefLabel`. A concept has exactly one preferred label per language.
Classification code for this concept within a scheme.
Formal definition of this concept. Optional for CDIF codelist concepts. A plain string.
Narrower (child) concepts. If present, each inline concept must also declare skos:broader pointing back to the parent concept. Both skos:narrower and skos:broader must be explicit in CDIF codelists.
Broader (parent) concepts. Required on any concept that appears as a skos:narrower value of another concept. CDIF requires both directions to be explicit for hierarchy traversal.

Catalog record describing this codelist as CDIF-conformant metadata. Must declare conformance to the cdifCodelist profile via dcterms:conformsTo and be typed as schema:Dataset with schema:additionalType including dcat:CatalogRecord.
Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.
Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).
Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.
A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.
the identifier string. E.g. 10.5066/F7VX0DMQ
web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ
text label for the term that is useful to human user
